title: HubSpot cuts 600 jobs as Indian American CEO accelerates AI pivot
key_facts: HubSpot announced plans to lay off about 600 employees, or 7% of its workforce.
CEO Yamini Rangan told staff in a letter that the strategy has shifted to delivering outcomes for customers with AI.
She said the layoffs are "not simply a cost-cutting exercise" and not driven by AI-related efficiencies; management layers will be cut.
Severance: 20 weeks of base pay plus one week per year of service up to 30 weeks, five months of health care and career support.
HubSpot reported Q2 revenue up 20% to nearly $912 million.
Layoffs.fyi counts 131,382 tech layoffs across 315 companies as of this week.
quote_evidence: Cambridge, Massachusetts-based technology company HubSpot announced plans to lay off about 600 employees, or 7% of its workforce, as the company pivots to a new AI-focused strategy.
Employees will receive 20 weeks of base pay, plus one week per year of service, up to a maximum of 30 weeks, in severance.
why_it_matters_hint: Another profitable software firm cuts staff while restructuring around AI.
event_date: about 6 Oct 2026 (Boston Globe and Quartz coverage dated 6 Oct)
notes: Quartz and others headline 660 jobs; the American Bazaar says about 600 (7%). Re-reported on 8 Oct; announced earlier, so score lowered one.
